claims.claim: The fixed-k problems are monotone under padding: k-Induced Disjoint Paths reduces to ℓ-Induced Disjoint Paths for every fixed ℓ≥k while preserving H3-freeness. Moreover, k=1 is linear-time solvable and every fixed-k problem is in NP.
claims.evidence: For ℓ≥k, take the disjoint union with ℓ−k copies of K2 and designate each new edge as a terminal pair. Each added pair has only its K2 edge as a path, so solutions correspond exactly. Since H3 is connected and has eight vertices, it cannot span components or occur inside a K2; H3-freeness is preserved in both directions. For k=1, connected terminals have a shortest path, and any chord would yield a shorter path, so reachability solves the problem in O(n+m). For fixed k, the path vertex sequences have polynomial size, and edges, endpoints, vertex-disjointness, chords, and inter-path adjacencies are polynomially checkable.
claims.witness: The padding gadget consists of an isolated K2 for every added terminal pair.
claims.search_method: Direct proof of every quantifier, supplemented by exhaustive testing of 10,650 graphs/terminal choices through five original vertices with two padding pairs.

claims.claim: Every H3-free graph is 6-degenerate, with the constant sharp; additionally, two vertices of degree at least three can never be at distance exactly three. Thus an n-vertex H3-free graph has at most 6n−21 edges for n≥7, and every connected H3-free graph of minimum degree at least three has diameter at most two.
claims.evidence: If u-x-y-v is a shortest three-edge path and deg(u),deg(v)≥3, shortestness puts two additional neighbors of each endpoint outside the connector. The two pairs are disjoint, since a common neighbor would give u and v distance at most two. These eight distinct vertices and the seven required edges form H3 as a subgraph; extra edges are irrelevant. For degeneracy, every minimum-degree-seven graph contains every eight-vertex tree: root the tree and embed parent-first; when the jth vertex is embedded, its parent has at most j−2≤6 already used neighbors and hence an unused neighbor. Thus any subgraph of minimum degree seven contains H3, proving 6-degeneracy. K7 proves sharpness. A degeneracy ordering contributes at most 6 edges per early vertex and at most 21 among its final seven vertices, giving 6n−21. Finally, the first and fourth vertices of any geodesic of length at least three contradict the distance-three result when minimum degree is at least three.
claims.witness: K7 is H3-free, has degeneracy 6, and has 21=6·7−21 edges. The checker also recognizes the explicit eight-vertex H3 with connector 0-1-2-3 and leaf pairs {4,5} and {6,7}.
claims.search_method: Independent extremal and metric proofs, followed by exact checks of the sharpness graph and forbidden-tree detector.

claims.claim: H3-free graphs admit an arbitrary-routing-plus-matching normal form. Let R be any graph and M a matching on V(R), disjoint from E(R). Replace every edge of R by a four-edge path and retain every edge of M unsubdivided, obtaining G(R,M). Then G(R,M) is H3-free. With all terminals in V(R), induced linkages in G(R,M) correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M such that every M-edge whose two endpoints are selected is itself used between consecutive vertices of one path. In particular, the H3-free class has unbounded treewidth.
claims.evidence: Every subdivision vertex has degree two, so an H3 center must be original. Leaving an original vertex through an R-corridor requires four edges to reach another original. Leaving through M reaches an original after one edge, but the matching condition precludes a second M-edge, and two subsequent corridor edges end at a subdivision vertex. Hence no three-edge connector can join possible centers, so no H3 occurs. A path with original endpoints must traverse each entered R-corridor completely; contraction therefore gives a simple path in R∪M, and lifting reverses it. Distinct lifted R-corridors introduce no extra adjacency. The only possible chord or inter-path edge is an unsubdivided M-edge, which is harmless exactly when it is the consecutive edge used by one path. With M empty and R=K_m, contracting the internally disjoint four-edge corridors gives a K_m minor, so treewidth is at least m−1.
claims.witness: For every m, M=∅ and R=K_m yields an H3-free four-edge subdivision containing K_m as a minor.
claims.search_method: Direct center-distance and projection/lifting proofs, plus exhaustive enumeration of all 9,984 disjoint routing-graph/matching constructions on five original vertices and 29,952 associated two-pair correspondence tests.

claims.claim: For arbitrary graphs, hence also for H3-free graphs, k-Induced Disjoint Paths is fixed-parameter tractable in k+b, where b is the number of vertices of degree at least three. There is an exact equivalent compression with at most b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices.
claims.evidence: Let B contain the b vertices of degree at least three. Every component of G−B is a path, isolated vertex, or cycle and has at most two attachment edges. A terminal-free component can participate only as a corridor between two distinct B vertices; same-end and dead-end components cannot occur in a simple terminal path. Corridors with the same unordered endpoints are interchangeable because their internal vertices have no other neighbors, so one two-edge representative per pair suffices. In a terminal-bearing component, mark terminals and B-attachment occurrences. Every solution either avoids or completely traverses each unmarked gap. A one-edge gap must remain an edge, while every gap of length at least two can be replaced by a two-edge path without changing endpoint adjacency, chords, inter-path edges, or liftability. A detached cycle containing exactly one terminal is an immediate NO case, closing the sketch's exceptional cyclic case. Retaining at most b+2k marked vertices, at most binom(b,2) generic representatives, and at most 4k gap representatives gives b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices: a terminal-bearing path component with t terminals has at most t+1≤2t gaps, and a cycle has t gaps. Exhaustive path enumeration on the compressed graph is a function only of k+b, while construction and lifting are polynomial, establishing FPT.
claims.witness: The certificate-preserving lift expands every compressed gap and generic corridor back to its chosen original degree-two path; multiple generic corridors with the same B endpoints are exchangeable.
claims.search_method: Complete structural case split, explicit treatment of dead ends, repeated endpoints, and one-terminal cycles, plus exhaustive equivalence testing on 68,800 instances through six vertices, including 194 forced-NO cyclic cases.

claims.claim: A globally shortest path for one terminal pair cannot be fixed greedily, even on a seven-vertex H3-free graph.
claims.evidence: H3 has eight vertices, so the stated seven-vertex graph is automatically H3-subgraph-free. Exact enumeration gives s1-x-t1 as the unique length-two, hence globally shortest, s1-t1 path. Every s2-t2 path contains s2, and xs2 is an edge, so no induced linkage can contain that shortest path. Conversely, s1-y-z-t1 together with s2-t2 is vertex-disjoint, each path is induced, and there is no edge between the two paths.
claims.witness: Vertices {s1,t1,x,s2,t2,y,z}; edges {s1x,xt1,xs2,s2t2,s1y,yz,zt1}. The valid linkage is (s1,y,z,t1) and (s2,t2); the incompatible unique shortest path is (s1,x,t1).
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of every simple terminal path and every compatible two-path linkage in the seven-vertex witness.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a complexity classification for every fixed k. The draft establishes polynomial time only for k=1. Padding gives monotonic implications but does not determine any k≥2; the structural results, FPT algorithm with the additional unbounded parameter b, and greedy counterexample likewise do not classify unrestricted H3-free instances for k≥2. Thus the draft makes material, correct progress but leaves the central classification open. Its claimed_resolution of PARTIAL and its explicit final disclaimer are accurate, neither overstated nor understated.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source input and baseline draft; used no web, retrieval database, treatment receipt, prior run, report, or other solution.
Reconstructed H3 from the target's definition as the eight-vertex tree whose degree-three centers are joined by a three-edge path.
Completed direct proofs for padding, degeneracy, the routing construction, compression, and the greedy counterexample, including omitted boundary cases.
Checked 10,650 padding instances, 9,984 routing hosts, 29,952 routing/linkage correspondences, and 68,800 compression instances with no mismatch.
Exactly enumerated the seven-vertex witness, confirming the valid longer linkage and incompatibility of the unique globally shortest path.
